title.narrative: Cabo Verde: Second Resilient and Equitable Recovery DPF with a Cat DDO

description.narrative: The program development objective is to support the Government's efforts to strengthen the foundations for a resilient and equitable economic recovery through (i) reducing fiscal risks and improving debt transparency; (ii) strengthening the resilience of poor and vulnerable households to climate shocks; and (iii) enabling a sustainable private sector-led recovery.

title.narrative: Result Indicator #8: New tourism investment projects approved in ZDTIs, in compliance with the corresponding POTs and with approved environmental impact assessments (% of total nbr of new ZDTI)

comment.narrative: Though no new tourism development plans were approved since the last mission, an important policy advance did take place as authorities created a major new batch of ZDTIs in two islands which had no such land banks. Through a Decree-Law effective March 3, 2025, nine (9) greenfield ZDTIs were created–3 in Santo Antão and 6 in São Nicolau islands–thus reflecting a policy drive and effort to spur investment in these two nascent tourism destinations. Following-up from recent advances on the licensing of tourism accommodations, the recent tourism-related regulatory drive in late 2025 has focused on enabling nautical tourism, including a forthcoming decree-law regulating concessions on recreational ports and marinas (supported through a World Bank IPF)–an important enabler to attract promoters to many of these greenfield ZDTIs.

title.narrative: Result Indicator #6: Additional households identified using the social registry that are from the two poorest quintiles

comment.narrative:
The Unified Social Registry (Cadastro Social Único - CSU) currently covers 64% of Cabo Verde's population and 59% of households. A total of 327,577 households are registered, of which 39,877 are classified in groups I and II (31% and 28%, respectively). At present, 16 social programs use the CSU as the basis for beneficiary selection and classification. (Portal CSU)
As of June 2025, there are additional 6,775 new registries of which 2,421 from groups I and II, bringing the total to 37,105 new registries in the CSU, of which 18,745 from groups I and II (50,5 percent). Despite the anticipated challenges in registering new households—particularly non-poor households—the expansion of the vocational education subsidy to all young people, regardless of group, has significantly boosted the number of new registrations. In parallel with the continuous registration of new poor households, the CSU has focused on updating expired records, with 73% of the database currently updated.

title.narrative: Result Indicator #3: Share of annual average loss from disaster and climate-related risks covered under the existing risk financing instruments

comment.narrative: For 2025, it was agreed to continue using the baseline of 2020, which estimated losses at US$18,2 million reported in Fiscal Risk Statement (FRS) for 2024. With assistance from the IMF, the Risk Management Unit (RMU) worked on complementing the annual average losses from droughts and floods with other hazards such as volcanic, seismic, sea level rise, etc. The quantification for 2026 amounts to ~US$30 million, which confirms the importance of complementing the FNE with the preparation of a new Cat DDO program, plus the consideration of additional disaster risk financing instruments.

title.narrative: Result Indicator #7: Improved ELECTRA's commercial operational performance: Overall system losses

comment.narrative: In 2025, overall system losses reached 22.7%, while efforts centered on consolidating the unbundling process through establishing contractual frameworks among new institutions and developing a tariff-setting methodology to enable commercially driven operations. A preliminary market sounding conducted between May-July 2025 engaged over 60 investors and financial institutions to gauge private sector interest in EDEC (distribution) and EPEC (thermal generation), assess reform structure and risk allocation, and identify strategic partners. Feedback indicated stronger interest in distribution assets compared to fossil fuel-based generation, particularly heavy fuel oil, though lenders expressed willingness to participate. The next phase requires intensive dialogue and road shows to engage strategic investors and finalize legal and regulatory frameworks.

title.narrative: Result Indicator #2: Support to SOEs (capitalization, guarantees, on-lending) above what is established in the annual budget (percentage)

comment.narrative: Since the introduction of reforms under the DPF series, the government has significantly reduced extraordinary support to the State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs) beyond the annual budget ceiling. This indicator declined from 8.9 percent in 2023 to 8 percent in 2024, reflecting stricter controls on capitalization, guarantees, along with sustained fiscal discipline and improved transparency. However, fiscal risks remain, requiring sustained oversight and integration of SOE debt into the MTDS and budget processes.

title.narrative: Result Indicator #4: Femaleheaded households benefitting from temporary income support in response to shocks, including climate-related, through emergency cash transfer programs (cumulative number)

comment.narrative:
Between 2023 and 2024 there was no allocation of the Emergency Social Inclusion Income (Rendimento Social de Inclusão Emergencial - RSIE), as no crisis mechanism was activated. The RSIE was activated for the recent State of Calamity in the islands of São Vicente, Santo Antão, and São Nicolau in August 2025, and the Government will report the numbers as soon as they are consolidated.
The regular Social Inclusion Income (RSI) remained active, benefiting, by June 2025, 6,316 new beneficiaries financed through the MAIS 2025 Fund, as well as 28 beneficiaries supported by the State Budget for the same year. In the coming two months, the figures will be updated with the integration of additional beneficiaries under the 2025 budget.

title.narrative: Result Indicator #9: Total investments generated in aquaculture – cumulative (USD million)

comment.narrative: The sector remains anchored around two private aquaculture initiatives in São Vicente, with no new investments recorded to date. The first, Fazenda de Camarão (an onshore shrimp farm established in 2010/2011), was the country's first aquaculture venture. The second, Nortuna, launched in 2021 by the Norwegian company NORTUNA SA in 2021, focuses on both onshore and offshore aquaculture of Atlantic Blue Fin Tuna (ABFT). Nortuna is also in advanced R&D phase, testing the commercial pilot production of Amberjack (Seriola rivoliana). The company's initial focus on ABFT continues to show strong commercial potential given its market value and growth prospects, and could unlock significant export opportunities if technical viability is confirmed. No further information is available regarding the status of fundraising for the US$10 million expansion phase to secure additional working capital for fish feed, offshore hatching and boating equipment.

title.narrative: Result Indicator #5: FNE audit report produced and published by the Court of Account including evaluation of drought response expenditures (yes/no).

comment.narrative: The Ministry of Finance confirmed that the audit by the General Inspection of Finances (IGF) is available for the year 2023 and that from 2022, all accounts have been published on the FNE website and delivered annually to the Court of Accounts, with the last accounts for 2024 delivered in May 2025. However, the Court of Accounts has not yet carried out or published its assessment. The Ministry of Finance also confirmed that the Government has no influence on the timeline or processes of the Court, and that the FNE has not been activated for drought-related response since the new bylaws under Decree-Law No. 59/2018. As part of the renewal of the Cat DDO, it is proposed to adjust this indicator to “FNE audit report produced by IGF and published in the FNE website (NA/Yes)”.

title.narrative: Result Indicator #1: Sectoral coverage score in the World Bank debt reporting heat map

comment.narrative: Cabo Verde has successfully achieved full sectoral coverage in the World Bank debt reporting heat map since 2022, ahead of the 2023 target. This marks a significant improvement from partial coverage in 2020, reflecting reforms supported under the DPF series to enhance debt transparency and fiscal risk management. As of October 2025, full coverage is sustained, strengthening the country's debt management framework and contributing to improved fiscal credibility.
